content:
As a Shortest mode clash it's useful for clashers to know whether you'll test any words ending in "di[^st]$" as those are an edge case that would cost you characters to handle (e.g. acadie, adil, affadir).

Your code would not exclude such words, but if your regex just demanded that "di\w$" was banned then it can just exclude all "di[st]$" words by also excluding "di[a-ru-z]$" with "di\w$" (lazy, but golfy).

I think it's best to not change test cases so long after a clash is submitted, so I'd suggest just updating the statement to clarify:
```
except if the word ends with>> {{di}}<<, or {{di?}} where {{?}} is any letter (e.g. words ending in >> {{dis}} <<or>> {{dit}}) (case-insensitive)
```
Nice clash! I love a RegEx friendly clash!

✅ Approved the contribution.
Comment: just be cuz i love string manipulation

"They will not include punctuation such as apostrophes," is stated in the statement, but the first testcase is "J'administre une distillerie proche de Lannion."

Is the punctuation after the character J an apostrophe, or does it mean other punctuation?

✅ Approved the contribution.
Comment: It's good:)

✅ Approved the contribution.
Comment: Nice problem!

I made this solution :

import re

mes = input().lower()
reg = r"di[^',. ]+"

mat = re.findall(reg, mes)

for mot in mat:
    if mot not in ["dis", "dit"]:
        reg2 = r"[\w]+"
        mat2 = re.search(reg2, mot[2:])
        if mat2 : 
            print(mat2.group())
            exit()

print("...")

Goal
* Please add "(case-insensitive)" after "dit".

* Please mention that words are always separated by a space.

Constraints
* Please add:
Words containing {{di}} or {{Di}} never have any punctuation marks attached.

Cases
* Currently, the validator inputs do not include the words "dis" and "Dis" (they're found in Tests 5 and 6 only). Please update the existing validators, or add new ones, to include these words.

* Please add a pair of cases where the message contains one or more words ending with "dis" (but not the word "dis" itself).

Thanks.

It shows I wrote this late, it needed quite some polish x_x

* Added examples.
* Added a strict definition of what a word is in this puzzle in the description rather than in the constraints.
* Added the "A bit dysfunctional" set of tests for words ending with "dis" not being "dis" itself.
* Added the word "dis" and "Dis" in the "Some dissonnance" and "In the middle" validators.

Wdyt now? :-)
Don't hesitate to approve if the puzzle meets CG standards, if you can :)

Ah dang, you're right, and I don't think I can remove the apostrophes easily from the test cases.

I've updated the sentence from the description:
> While the sentence can contain apostrophes, the word to process, if present, will not contain any.

How about now? :)

Very good remark! I disagree with the fact that changing test cases is a bad idea: it's only a bad idea if you want to deal with people copying solutions from previous runs, which IMO is against the spirit of the game.

I've added the "acadie" example for single-letter follow-ups, and the "Dig!" test case pair to test this single-letter follow-up case.

Thanks a lot :)
